sanskrit: kena devām̐ anu kṣiyati kena daivīr ajanayad diśaḥ | kenedam anyan nakṣatraṃ kena sat kṣatram ucyate ||
english: By what does one dwell in the wake of the gods? By what did he bring forth the divine directions? By what this other constellation? By what is the existent called the ruling power?

sanskrit: kena parjanyam āpnoti kena somaṃ vicakṣaṇam | kenemam agniṃ puruṣaḥ kena saṃvatsaraṃ mame ||
english: By what does one attain Parjanya? By what the far-seeing Soma? By what does a man attain this Agni? By what does he measure out the year?

sanskrit: keneyaṃ bhūmir nihitā kena dyaur uttarā hitā | kenedam ūrdhvaṃ tiryak ca- -antarikṣaṃ vyaco hitam ||
english: By what was this earth set in place? By what was the upper heaven established? By what was this atmosphere—both upward-reaching and transverse—spread wide and set in position?

sanskrit: brahmaṇā bhūmir nihitā brahma dyām uttarāṃ dadhau | brahmedam ūrdhvaṃ tiryak ca- -antarikṣaṃ vyaco hitam ||
english: By Brahman was the earth set in place; Brahman upheld the upper heaven; by Brahman was this atmosphere—both upward-reaching and transverse—spread wide and set in position.

sanskrit: kena śrotriyam āpnoti kenemaṃ parameṣṭhinam | kena yajñaś ca śraddhā ca kenāsmin nihitaṃ manaḥ ||
english: By what does one attain the Vedic scholar? By what this Parameṣṭhin? By what sacrifice and faith? By what is mind established within him?

sanskrit: brahma śrotriyam āpnoti brahmemaṃ parameṣṭhinam | brahma yajñaś ca śraddhā ca brahmāsmin nihitaṃ manaḥ ||
english: By Brahman one attains the Vedic scholar; Brahman is this Parameṣṭhin; Brahman is sacrifice and faith; by Brahman is mind established within him.

sanskrit: ka idam asthy asṛjata ka idaṃ māṃsaṃ sam abharat | ka imāṃ tvacaṃ ca loma ca ka idaṃ rūpaṃ sam airayat ||
english: Who created these bones? Who assembled this flesh? Who gathered this skin and hair? Who put together this form?

sanskrit: brahmāsthy asṛjata brahma māṃsaṃ sam abharat | brahma tvacaṃ ca loma ca brahma rūpaṃ sam airayat ||
english: Brahman created the bones; Brahman assembled the flesh; Brahman gathered skin and hair; Brahman put together the form.

sanskrit: ka idaṃ cakṣur asṛjata kaḥ prāṇaṃ kheṣv āvayat | ka idaṃ manaś ca vācaṃ ca ka imāṃ sam abharat puram ||
english: Who created this eye? Who set the breath moving through the apertures? Who gathered this mind and speech? Who assembled this citadel?

sanskrit: brahma cakṣur asṛjata brahma khe prāṇam āvayat | brahma manaś ca vācaṃ ca brahma sam abharat puram ||
english: Brahman created the eye; Brahman set the breath moving through the aperture; Brahman gathered mind and speech; Brahman assembled this citadel.

sanskrit: nainaṃ cakṣur jahāti na prāṇo jarasaḥ puraḥ | puraṃ yo brahmaṇo veda yasmāt puruṣa ucyate ||
english: The eye does not abandon him, nor does the breath, before old age, for he who knows the citadel of Brahman—it is on that account that he is called Puruṣa.

sanskrit: yo vai tāṃ brahmaṇo veda- -amṛtenāvṛtāṃ puram | tasmai brahma ca brāhmyāś ca- -āyuṣ prāṇaṃ prajāṃ daduḥ ||
english: To him who truly knows that citadel of Brahman enveloped in immortality, both Brahman and the Brahmic powers have given life-span, breath, and progeny.

sanskrit: aṣṭācakrā navadvārā devāṇāṃ pūr ayodhyā | tasyāṃ hiraṇyayaḥ kośaḥ svargo jyotiṣāvṛtaḥ ||
english: Eight-wheeled, nine-gated is the unconquerable citadel of the gods; within it is a golden sheath enveloped in the light of heaven.

sanskrit: tasmin hiraṇyaye kośe tryare tripratiṣṭhite | tasmin yad antar ātmanvat tad vai brahmavido viduḥ ||
english: In that golden sheath with three spokes, set on three supports—that which abides within it, possessing the Self, that indeed the knowers of Brahman know.

sanskrit: prabhrājamānāṃ hariṇīṃ yaśasā saṃparīvṛtām | puraṃ hiraṇmayīṃ brahmā viveśāparājitām ||
english: The golden, resplendent, tawny citadel, enveloped in glory, unconquered—into it did Brahmā enter.

sanskrit: ayaṃ te varaṇo maṇiḥ sapatnakṣayaṇaḥ kṛtaḥ | tenā rabhasva tvaṃ śatrūn pra mṛṇīhi durasyataḥ ||
english: This varaṇa-amulet of yours has been fashioned as the destroyer of rivals; with it seize your enemies boldly, crush down those who scheme you harm.

sanskrit: aināñ chṛṇīhi pra mṛṇā rabhasva maṇis te astu puraetā purastāt | avārayanta varaṇena devā abhyācāram asurāṇāṃ śvaḥśvaḥ ||
english: Smite them, crush them down, attack them boldly—let the amulet be your vanguard going before you! The gods, day by day, warded off with the varaṇa the onslaughts of the Asuras.

sanskrit: ā tvārakṣad varaṇo viśvabheṣajaḥ sahasrākṣo harito hiraṇyayaḥ | yas te śatrūn adharān pātayāsi pūrvas tān dabhnuhi ya u tvā dviṣanti ||
english: The varaṇa—all-healing, thousand-eyed, green-hued, golden—has enclosed you in protection; you who strike your enemies down, overwhelm them first, those who indeed hate you.

sanskrit: ayaṃ te kṛtyāṃ vitatāṃ pauruṣeyam ayaṃ vadham | ayaṃ te sarvaṃ pāpmānaṃ varaṇo vārayiṣyate ||
english: This varaṇa shall ward off for you the widely spread sorcery, the man-made harm; this shall ward off all evil from you.

sanskrit: varaṇo vārayātā idaṃ devo vanaspatiḥ | yakṣmaḥ praviṣṭo yo 'smin tam u devā avīvaran ||
english: Let the divine varaṇa, lord of the forest, ward off this; the disease that has entered into him—that the gods have shielded against with the varaṇa.

sanskrit: svapnaṃ suptvā yadi paśyāsi pāpaṃ mṛgaḥ sṛtiṃ yati dhāvād ajuṣṭām | parikṣavāc chakuneḥ pāpavādād ayaṃ maṇir varaṇo vārayātai ||
english: If on sleeping you behold an evil dream, if a beast runs off on an ill-omened track—from ill-boding sneezing, from an evil omen of a bird, let this varaṇa amulet ward off all.

sanskrit: arātyā mā nirṛtyā abhicārād atho bhayāt | mṛtyor ojīyaso vadhāt tvaṃ varaṇa vāraya ||
english: From malice, from Nirṛti, from sorcery, and from fear; from the blow of a death mightier than death—from these, O Varaṇa, ward me off.

sanskrit: varaṇena pravyathitā bhrātṛvyā me sabandhavaḥ | asūrtaṃ rajo 'py agus te yantv adhamaṃ tamaḥ ||
english: My adversaries and their kinsmen, shaken to pieces by the varaṇa—into the formless darkness, into the realm of non-being, let them go into the lowest gloom.

sanskrit: yan me mātā yan me pitā bhrātaro yac ca me svā yad enaś cakṛmā vayam | tasmān no vārayiṣyate 'yaṃ devo vanaspatiḥ ||
english: Whatever sin my mother has committed, whatever my father, my brothers, our own people—whatever transgression we have done—from that shall this divine lord of the forest ward us off.

sanskrit: ariṣṭo 'ham ariṣṭagur āyuṣmān sarvapūruṣaḥ | taṃ māyaṃ varaṇo maṇiḥ pari pātu diśodiśaḥ ||
english: Unharmed am I, unharmed in my cattle, long-lived, complete in all my being—me, thus, let the varaṇa amulet guard on every side, from all directions.
